question: A farmer presents with a corneal ulcer after a twig injury to the right eye. Slit-lamp shows a dry, rough-surfaced ulcer with feathery edges and satellite lesions. KOH mount reveals branching septate hyphae. Which is the FIRST-LINE topical treatment?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Acyclovir is antiviral — specific for HSV keratitis (dendritic/geographic ulcer). This patient has fungal keratitis (trauma + hyphae on KOH). Acyclovir has no antifungal activity.

Correct. Natamycin 5% is first-line for filamentous fungal keratitis (Fusarium, Aspergillus) — the most common fungi after vegetative trauma in India. It is a polyene antifungal with broad spectrum against filamentous fungi.
Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone (antibacterial) with no antifungal activity. Bacterial keratitis typically shows a grey-white ulcer with suppuration, not feathery edges or hyphae on KOH.

Voriconazole is a useful second-line antifungal (triazole class), especially for Candida and resistant filamentous fungi. However, natamycin 5% remains the recommended first-line agent for filamentous fungal keratitis per Indian guidelines.

overallFeedback.feedback: Filamentous fungal keratitis (Fusarium/Aspergillus after vegetative trauma) = natamycin 5% first-line. Distinguish from: HSV → acyclovir; bacterial → fluoroquinolone; Candida → voriconazole.

Correct! Vegetative trauma + feathery edges + hyphae → fungal keratitis → natamycin 5% first-line. Remember the mnemonic: 'Natamycin for farmers (filamentous); voriconazole for failures (resistant cases)'.
